en-US.author: jdx
en-US.longDescription: Your dev env, already prepped. One tool to manage languages, env vars, and tasks per project, reproducibly.
en-US.name: mise-en-place
en-US.releaseNotes:
The default 24-hour minimum_release_age now applies to every backend. Many more backends report release dates, so the cooldown can actually hold new versions back, and mise warns when it installs a version it couldn't date. This release also adds a PowerShell installer for Windows, read_json/read_yaml/read_toml template functions, dotnet@lts/dotnet@sts, and new dotfiles options.
Changed
- The default minimum_release_age applies to every backend. The built-in 24h cooldown used to cover only backends that reported release dates (aqua, cargo, core, github, npm, pypi and others). asdf, vfox, conda, dotnet, http: and s3: tools had no cutoff at all. Now every backend gets the cooldown. A tool whose only version is less than 24h old now resolves to "no versions found", as aqua and github tools already did. To opt a tool out, add it to minimum_release_age_excludes. To turn the cooldown off, set minimum_release_age = "0s". #14701 (@jdx)
- mise warns when it can't check a version's release date. A version with no known date still passes the cutoff, but mise install, mise upgrade and mise use now print a one-time warning naming the version. Exact pins you wrote yourself don't trigger it. mise env, mise ls, mise outdated and mise ls-remote never print it. #14694 (@jdx)
  WARN  asdf:tiny@3.1.0 has no release date, so the ... cutoff cannot be checked and it is allowed (exclude it with minimum_release_age_excludes to silence this)
- More backends report release dates, so the cooldown applies to them:
  - conda versions use the channel's earliest index timestamp. #14693
  - aqua packages that take versions from git tags (version_source: github_tag, such as aws/aws-cli, docker/cli and cockroachdb/cockroach) are now dated. #14691
  - dotnet dates come from Microsoft's releases index. deno and erlang dates come from their GitHub releases. #14692
  - Every python version now has a date, and so do many more ruby versions (from ruby-lang.org, Maven Central for JRuby, and GitHub for TruffleRuby). Rust's stable, beta and nightly channels are dated too. With an explicit past cutoff, rust@stable resolves to the newest stable release that is old enough, and beta/nightly resolve to a dated build from before the cutoff. #14697
  - The dart, flutter, nim, julia, nomad-pack, sentinel, tfc-agent, android-cli, cursor-agent and twg registry tools now report dates. #14698
  All by @jdx.
- Version lists for more backends come from the mise-versions host. npm:, pipx:, cargo:, gem:, go:, dotnet: and spm: tools now list versions from mise-versions, like other registry tools, instead of going to their own source. So do http/s3 tools with a version_list_url. If you redirect a source, mise still lists from that source directly. That covers a custom npm registry or npm.shell_out, pypi.registry_url, a non-default GOPROXY, cargo.registry_name, a custom gem source, dotnet.registry_url, S3 endpoint overrides, and local listing options. conda always lists from its channel. The host cache TTL now follows the tool's minimum_release_age. To list everything from the source, set MISE_USE_VERSIONS_HOST=0. #14700 (@jdx)

Added
- PowerShell installer for Windows. It's published with each release as install.ps1 and served from mise.run at /powershell and /pwsh, so you pipe it into iex with irm. It works on PowerShell 5.1+ and doesn't need admin rights. It installs the newest release that is at least 24h old, or MISE_VERSION if set. The download is verified against SHASUMS256.txt from GitHub Releases. mise.exe and mise-shim.exe go into ~\.local\bin, and that directory is added to your user Path. Re-running it upgrades an existing install. Options include MISE_INSTALL_PATH, MISE_INSTALL_MODIFY_PATH=0, MISE_INSTALL_SHIMS_PATH=1 and MISE_INSTALL_FROM_GITHUB=1. See the "Installing mise" docs for the full command. #14660 (@jdx, @lhs-12)
- read_json(), read_yaml() and read_toml() template functions parse a file so a template can use a value from it. This saves copying a version from package.json or Pulumi.yaml into mise.toml by hand. Relative paths resolve from the config file's directory. A missing key is an error unless you add | default(value="..."). Like read_file(), these functions need a trusted config, and they don't work in safe mode, .miserc.toml or OCI dotfile templates. #14705 (@jdx, @edahlseng)
  [tools]
  node = "{{ read_json(path='package.json')['volta']['node'] }}"
  pulumi = "{{ read_yaml(path='Pulumi.yaml')['requiredPulumiVersion'] }}"
- dotnet@lts and dotnet@sts resolve to the newest SDK in the current LTS or STS channel, using Microsoft's release index. Preview, go-live and end-of-life channels are skipped. A lts alias you define in [tool_alias.dotnet.versions] still takes precedence. Runtime-only installs still need an exact version. #14683 (@jdx)
- mise bootstrap --prune-dotfiles removes dotfiles that are no longer deployed, the same way mise dot apply --prune does, so mise bootstrap --upgrade --prune-dotfiles handles everything in one run. The prune runs at the end of the dotfiles phase. It respects --dry-run, --yes and --skip dotfiles. Copies you edited are left in place. #14681 (@jdx, @thernstig)
- dotfiles.windows_symlinks (default false) makes symlink and symlink-each create real file symlinks on Windows. With it on, apply fails if Windows refuses to create a link, instead of silently copying. To create symlinks, Windows needs Developer Mode or an elevated shell. If you turn the setting back off, mise dot unapply needs --force on entries that still hold links. #14682 (@jdx)
  [settings.dotfiles]
  windows_symlinks = true
- http: tools can report release dates with the new version_date_expr option. It maps versions to dates from the version_list_url response. Use version_date_url to read the dates from a different URL, and version_date_next_expr to follow paged listings (same host only). Dates can be RFC 3339, YYYY-MM-DD or HTTP dates. #14696 (@jdx)
- vfox plugins can report release dates. An Available or BackendListVersions hook can return created_at (RFC 3339) for each version. Plain version strings still work. #14695 (@jdx)
- mise tasks -a is a short alias for mise tasks --all. #14674 (@williamsjokvist)

Fixed
- mise fmt no longer breaks multiline inline tables (TOML 1.1). It used to pull comments out of the table and drop indentation. Now it leaves these tables exactly as written. #14670 (@jdx, @ponko2)
- If one task's dir template fails to render, other task commands keep working. Before, every command failed, including mise tasks validate. Now mise tasks validate reports the broken task as invalid-directory-template, and only running that task fails. #14680 (@jdx)
- aqua tools now find their binaries in macOS universal archives, such as fastfetch 2.70.0. #14665 (@jdx)
- npm: lifecycle scripts approved by allow_builds now run even when ~/.npmrc sets ignore-scripts=true. #14661 (@jdx)
- npm: mise lock no longer fails when your aube config sets a different default lockfile, such as pnpm-lock.yaml. #14659 (@jdx)
- .7z tool archives now extract when mise's data directory path contains .., for example in a localized mise setup. #14657 (@jdx, @sevenc-nanashi)
- The mise-shim.exe in the Windows release now keeps its version tag, so mise doctor and mise reshim --force stop reporting it as outdated. The warning goes away after you update and run mise reshim --force. #14656 (@jdx)
- On Windows, symlink-each dotfiles messages and dry-run previews now say the files were copied rather than symlinked. #14654 (@jdx, @lhs-12)
- Rust: with a RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER mirror configured and GitHub unreachable, mise now lists the stable, beta and nightly channels instead of failing, so rust@stable installs through the mirror. #14662 (@jdx)
- On Windows, http: installs of large archives no longer fail with "Access is denied" while antivirus is scanning the extracted files. mise now retries the final move for up to about a minute. #14703 (@jdx)

Documentation
- New mise.toml playground: a schema-aware editor with hover help, completion and error checking. You can share a config as a link. Every mise.toml example in the docs now shows hover help on its keys. #14673, #14686 (@jdx)
- The mise.toml reference is now a searchable key explorer grouped by topic. Each key shows its type, default and a real example. Nearly every key now has a description, and these also appear in mise config explain. #14687, #14690, #14688 (@jdx)
- The fnox secrets page now covers setup, CI and migration. The dotnet page explains how private feeds authenticate. #14675, #14679 (@jdx)
